questions.question: In right △ABC with ∠B = 90°, AB = 9 cm and BC = 12 cm. The length of hypotenuse AC (in cm) is ____.
questions.method_hint: In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is opposite the right angle. Use a² + b² = c² where c is the hypotenuse.

questions.question: In right △PQR with ∠Q = 90°, PQ = 5 cm and PR = 13 cm. The length of QR (in cm) is ____.
questions.method_hint: If the hypotenuse and one leg are known, rearrange a² + b² = c² to find the other leg: b² = c² − a².

questions.question: In right △XYZ with ∠Y = 90°, XY = 8 cm and YZ = 15 cm. The length of XZ (in cm) is ____.
questions.method_hint: Square both legs, add the squares, then take the positive square root to get the hypotenuse.

questions.question: In right △DEF with ∠E = 90°, DE = 7 cm and DF = 25 cm. The length of EF (in cm) is ____.
questions.method_hint: Hypotenuse is DF. Find the other leg using leg² = hypotenuse² − known leg².

questions.question: In right △LMN with ∠M = 90°, LM = 20 cm and MN = 21 cm. The length of LN (in cm) is ____.
questions.method_hint: Apply a² + b² = c² with the two legs LM and MN; LN is the hypotenuse.

questions.question: In right △ABC with ∠C = 90°, AC = 9 cm and BC = 40 cm. The length of AB (in cm) is ____.
questions.method_hint: With right angle at C, AB is the hypotenuse. Compute √(AC² + BC²).

questions.question: In right △RST with ∠S = 90°, RS = 11 cm and ST = 60 cm. The length of RT (in cm) is ____.
questions.method_hint: Add the squares of the two legs, then take the square root for the hypotenuse.

questions.question: If the sides of a triangle are 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm, then a² + b² − c² (taking c as the longest side) equals ____.
questions.method_hint: For sides satisfying the Baudhayana–Pythagoras relation, a² + b² = c², so a² + b² − c² = 0 when c is the longest side.

questions.question: The sides of a right triangle are in the ratio 5 : 12 : 13. If the shortest side is 15 cm, the hypotenuse (in cm) is ____.
questions.method_hint: Scale the Pythagorean triple by the same factor so the shortest side matches the given length; the hypotenuse scales by that factor.
questions.explanation: Shortest part of 5 : 12 : 13 is 5. Scale factor = 15/5 = 3. Hypotenuse = 13 × 3 = 39

questions.question: One leg of a right triangle is 16 cm and the hypotenuse is 34 cm. The other leg (in cm) is ____.
questions.method_hint: Use b² = c² − a², then take the positive square root.

questions.question: If a² + b² = c² with a = 9 and c = 15, then b equals ____.
questions.method_hint: Rearrange to b² = c² − a² and solve for the positive value of b.

questions.question: For legs 14 cm and 48 cm of a right triangle, the hypotenuse (in cm) is ____.
questions.method_hint: Compute √(a² + b²) using the two given legs.

questions.question: A ladder leans against a wall. The foot of the ladder is 9 m from the wall and the top reaches 12 m up the wall. The length of the ladder (in m) is ____.
questions.method_hint: The wall, ground and ladder form a right triangle. The ladder is the hypotenuse.

questions.question: A vertical pole is 8 m high. A wire from the top of the pole to a point on the ground 15 m from the foot of the pole is stretched tight. The length of the wire (in m) is ____.
questions.method_hint: Pole and ground meet at right angles; the wire is the hypotenuse of that right triangle.

questions.question: A rectangular park is 40 m long and 9 m wide. The length of a straight path joining opposite corners (in m) is ____.
questions.method_hint: The diagonal of a rectangle is the hypotenuse of a right triangle formed by length and breadth.

questions.question: From a point on the ground 24 m away from the base of a tower, the distance to the top of the tower is 25 m. The height of the tower (in m) is ____.
questions.method_hint: Height, base distance and slant distance form a right triangle; height² = slant² − base².

questions.question: A ship sails 20 km due east and then 21 km due north. Its straight-line distance from the starting point (in km) is ____.
questions.method_hint: East and north displacements are perpendicular. Use a² + b² = c² for the straight-line distance.

questions.question: In a right triangle, one leg is 12 cm and the hypotenuse is 37 cm. The other leg (in cm) is ____.
questions.method_hint: Apply the Baudhayana–Pythagoras theorem: other leg² = hypotenuse² − known leg².

questions.question: The sides of a triangle are 9 cm, 40 cm and 41 cm. The value of a² + b² when a and b are the two shorter sides is ____.
questions.method_hint: Square each of the two shorter sides and add. For a right triangle this equals the square of the longest side.

questions.question: A square has side 15 cm. The length of one diagonal of the square (in cm) is ____.
questions.method_hint: A diagonal of a square of side s satisfies d² = s² + s² = 2s², so d = s√2. Use √2 ≈ 1.414.
